summary: Announced the death of President William McKinley and named Thursday, September 19, 1901, the day of his burial, a national day of mourning and prayer.
Enlarged the Fort Sill Military Reservation in Comanche County, Oklahoma Territory, by 893.07 acres so certain Apache prisoners of war could be located there.
Shrank a Colorado forest reserve (printed as Black Mesa, but the lands lie in the Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve) and returned the described lands to the public domain.
Named T. S. Sharretts special appraiser of duties on imports into China.
Set the ratings and pay of petty officers and other enlisted men in the Navy's Commissary Branch.
Reserved Harbor Island and three islets southeast of it in Sitka Harbor, Alaska, for the Revenue Cutter Service.
Let the vacancy for the clerk who signs checks for the pension agent at the Philadelphia pension agency be filled without a civil-service examination.
Allowed the vacant post of White House steward to be filled without a civil-service examination.
Set apart Thursday, November 28, 1901, as a day of national thanksgiving, while noting the country still mourned President McKinley.
Allowed the Navy Department to fill a vacant laborer job, with the duties of coachman in the Assistant Secretary of the Navy's office, without a civil-service examination.
Reserved certain lands in Zambales and Bataan, on the island of Luzon in the Philippines, for naval purposes.
Set aside described lands near Point Dume, California, for a lighthouse, subject to any legal existing rights.
Withdrew described lands in Arizona Territory next to the Moqui and Navajo reservations from sale, holding them until the Indians living there could settle them as homesteads.
Reserved San Nicolas Island, off California, for lighthouse purposes.
Amended Civil Service Rule III by striking four clauses, (g) through (j), from its list of exceptions, bringing certain U.S. Army positions under classification.

Changed the civil-service rules so that when an Indian training school superintendent took over an agency's duties, the displaced Indian agent could be made a classified employee after a fitness test.
Amended the civil-service transfer rule so apportionment limits "may" (rather than "shall") be waived, and only with a detailed certificate approved by the Civil Service Commission.
Granted enlisted men of the Navy extra monthly pay for good conduct.

Redefined the classified Post-Office Service to cover employees of free-delivery post offices and rural free delivery, with rural carriers held outside classification until their appointment regulations took effect.
Gave Navy enlisted men who held petty officers' training certificates additional pay.
Authorized a classification and monthly pay scale for Navy mess attendants.

Set a procedure for removing people holding jobs in violation of the civil-service law: after notice, the Commission certifies the violation, and pay stops if the person isn't dismissed within thirty days.
Required every federal officer and employee to give the Civil Service Commission information and sworn testimony in its investigations.
Barred transfers of civil servants who had not served at least six months in the office where they became classified.
Let appointing officers hire from a register holding only one or two eligible candidates, as if a full list of three had been certified.
Placed described lands on Culebra Island, off Puerto Rico, under the jurisdiction of the Navy Department, subject to existing private rights.
Set separate civil-service age limits for rural letter carriers, ages 17 to 55, while keeping 18 to 45 for all other Post-Office positions.
Waived the age limits for honorably discharged Civil War and Spanish-American War soldiers and sailors applying to be rural letter carriers.
Gave honorably discharged Civil War veterans, if fit and qualified, preference in being hired and kept in government jobs.
Allowed the vacant post of Assistant Commissioner of Immigration at the Port of New York to be filled without examination.
Amended the civil-service rules on which Navy Department draftsmen are excepted from examination.
Shrank the Oklahoma City Land District in Oklahoma Territory, moving described lands into the El Reno and Mangum land districts.
Abolished the Perry Land District and land office in Oklahoma Territory and moved its lands, records and business to the Guthrie office.
Closed the Enid Land District and land office in Oklahoma Territory, handing its lands, records and business to the Kingfisher office.
Added civil-service age limits for watch officers (21 to 36) and chief engineers (25 to 45) in the Coast and Geodetic Survey.
Excepted four special inspectors in the Interior Department from civil-service examination, alongside the one special land inspector already excepted.
Struck the civil-service provision that let people dismissed for misconduct be reinstated beyond the one-year limit if the charges proved untrue.
Limited civil-service transfers to positions requiring the same class of work or the same mechanical trade as the employee's current job.

Ordered appointing officers in Washington's executive departments to give the Civil Service Commission detailed lists of every position treated as unclassified, so the Commission could decide each one's status.
Rewrote the rules for emergency and temporary appointments, limiting emergency hires to thirty days a year and requiring them to be reported to the Civil Service Commission.
Named a reception committee for the visit of Prince Henry of Prussia.
Forbade federal executive employees, alone or through associations, from seeking pay raises or lobbying Congress in their own interest except through their department heads, on penalty of dismissal.
Let certain Bureau of Engraving and Printing workers transfer without examination to money-counting and sorting jobs elsewhere in the Treasury, with limited later rights.
Allowed John P. Green of Ohio, postage-stamp agent in the Post-Office Department since 1897, to be treated as holding a competitive position without examination.

Updated the list of quarantine stations whose Marine-Hospital Service attendants are excepted from classification, and added temporary acting assistant surgeons and sanitary inspectors during epidemics.
Moved the Office of the Surveyor-General of Arizona Territory from Tucson to Phoenix.
Made Albert H. Clark, injured in the line of duty, eligible for appointment as an assistant messenger in the War Department.
Revised the consular regulations on currency certificates for import invoices, letting a friendly nation's consul or two respectable merchants issue the certificate when they certify the invoice.
Required people whose jobs became classified to pass the entrance examination before transferring to another department, office or branch.
Barred reinstated federal employees from transferring until they had served six months in the office where they were reinstated.

Approved the Civil Service Commission's recommendation to suspend the twenty-year age limit for Richard D. Micou and others who passed the computer exam for the Naval Observatory and Nautical Almanac Office.
Barred consular officers from accepting appointment by a foreign state as administrator, guardian or other estate fiduciary without prior approval from the Secretary of State.
Reserved an office building and a 200-foot-square tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Arizona Territory, for the Weather Bureau.
Ordered flags at half-mast on all federal buildings in honor of the late Lord Pauncefote, the British Ambassador.
Created a single Juneau Land District covering all of Alaska, opening June 2, 1902, and closed the Circle, Sitka and Yukon land districts and their offices on May 31.
Created the San Isabel Forest Reserve in Colorado, setting the described timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.
Established the Santa Rita Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, closing the described timbered public lands to entry and settlement.
Established the Manila Bay Military Reservations in the Philippines, about 180 square miles at Mariveles, Calumpan Point and the islands and rocks between them in Bataan and Cavite provinces.
Consolidated the San Francisco Mountains Forest Reserves in Arizona Territory into a single reserve and added adjacent timbered lands to it.
Set apart the Niobrara Forest Reserve in Nebraska, reserving the described public lands from entry and settlement.
Created the Dismal River Forest Reserve in Nebraska from described public lands, closing them to entry and settlement.
Forbade diplomatic and consular officers from publicly attacking or criticizing one another; any charges had to go confidentially to the State Department.
Ordered flags at half-mast on all federal buildings for the late J. Sterling Morton, former Secretary of Agriculture.
Reserved a residence building and described tract in the abandoned Fort Yuma Military Reservation, Arizona Territory, for the Customs Service.
Placed Navy special mechanics, civilian inspectors and draftsmen under Navy Department labor regulations, with appointments made on navy-yard fitness tests instead of civil-service examinations.
Reserved described lands near Point Dume, California, for lighthouse purposes, subject to any legal existing rights.
Appointed William B. Dunlany messenger in the office of the Secretary to the President without examination, citing his "peculiar qualifications."
Opened to settlement the lands of the Fort Hall Indian Reservation in Idaho that the Shoshone and Bannock Indians had ceded to the United States under an agreement ratified in 1900.
Excused Spanish-American War veterans in federal jobs in the District of Columbia from duty on May 21 to attend the dedication of the statue to the war's dead at Arlington Cemetery.
Gave Civil War veterans in federal jobs in the District of Columbia the day off on May 17 to attend the reburial of Major General W. S. Rosecrans.
Replaced the Yellowstone Park Timber Land Reserve and the earlier Teton Forest Reserve in Wyoming with newly bounded Yellowstone and Teton forest reserves.
Established the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve in Wyoming, closing the described timbered public lands to entry and settlement.
Enlarged the Big Horn Forest Reserve in Wyoming, adding described townships and reserving them from entry or settlement.
Restored Section 7, Township 15 South, Range 2 East, San Bernardino Meridian, California, to the public domain, removing it from lands once reserved for the Captain Grande band of Mission Indians.
Defined "just cause" for removal from the classified civil service as any cause, other than a merely political or religious one, that promotes the efficiency of the service.
Reserved Lot 1 of Block 40 in Alva, Oklahoma Territory, for post office purposes.
Allowed the vacancy for Assistant Commissioner of Immigration at the port of New York to be filled without a civil-service examination.
Established a coal depot on Amaknak Island, Alaska, on lands reserved for lighthouse purposes in 1899.
Added described lands in Wyoming to the Yellowstone Forest Reserve, reserving them from entry or settlement.
Established the San Felipe Pueblo Indian Reservation in New Mexico Territory for the Indians of the Pueblo of San Felipe, subject to valid existing rights.
Redrew the boundary between the WaKeeney and Colby land districts in Kansas.
Reserved described lands in Kitsap County, Washington, for a Navy target range.
Reserved certain lands on Adak and Kiska islands, Alaska, for naval purposes.
Let the Justice Department fill its vacant disbursing-clerk job by transferring Alexander C. Caine from his excepted post as examiner, without regard to civil-service rules.
Returned 38.6 acres once reserved for the Kiowa and Comanche Indian Agency to the public domain, so the adjoining city of Anadarko, Oklahoma Territory, could acquire it for a park.
Redrew the boundaries of the White River Plateau Timber Land Reserve in Colorado and renamed it the White River Forest Reserve.
Opened the copperplate map engraver examination to foreign-born applicants who had declared their intention to become U.S. citizens, to supply enough eligibles.
Formally proclaimed the new schedule for the Louisiana Purchase Exposition in St. Louis: buildings dedicated by April 30, 1903, and opening to visitors no later than May 1, 1904.
Created the Santa Catalina Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, setting the described timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.
Suspended discriminating tonnage and import duties on Cuban vessels and their cargoes in U.S. ports, for as long as Cuba exempted American vessels from such duties.
Ruled that only an employee's supervisors may recommend promotions; outside recommendations made with the employee's knowledge could bar the promotion, and a repeat could mean removal.
Ordered that unclassified laborers in executive departments and independent offices be hired under regulations approved by department heads and the Civil Service Commission.
Allowed certain former employees of the U.S. military government in Cuba, commended for service amid danger from yellow fever and other tropical diseases, to be appointed in the classified service.
Granted full pardon and amnesty to people in the Philippines who took part in, or aided, the insurrections against Spain and the United States, with exceptions and excluding the Moro country.
Established regulations for discharging Navy enlisted men before the end of their terms.
